chapter: Own groups, bebop and Savoy sessions
title: The Dizzy Gillespie and Charlie Parker session of 1945

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Well of course there's one thing we have to talk about, was the session that you did with Bird and Dizzy. And Reno Pamieri and Clyde Hart and Slam Stewart. And that was 1945.
And what was the boy who was drumming with them before?
Sid Catlett did a record with them.
Yeah, but this was another boy. God, I'm just bad on names.
No, boy out of Chicago. Well anyway he didn't show on the recording date, so Diz and Burt called me and that's how I happened to do it.
Did you meet them on 52nd Street?
I know Diz you know from Calloway's band but Bird.
I met Bird yeah on 52nd Street, down around there.
Dizzy must have thought a lot of you to have you on a record like that.

Oh yeah. Yeah, Diz called me, said, Cozy, our drummer--what was his name--said he never showed. Can you make it? I said, yeah. He said drums are already here, so I didn't have to bring any drums. He said bring your sticks and brushes. So I did.
